vectors.note: a premove timed before the slot's anchor costs the mover no clock time
a move played in order charges timing - anchor
boundary: timing exactly at the anchor charges zero
abandonment timeout: the on-move player is charged from the last anchor to the cutoff (here the timing field carries the cutoff)
first half-move charges from t0 (anchor = t0)

sequences.note: strictly increasing timings charge their deltas, alternating sides; the anchor ends at the last timing

the d0229f… law seen from the clock split: the applied premove (chain position 3, timed 50 — BEFORE its predecessor's 55) charges zero, and the anchor NEVER REWINDS to 50 — the next mover is billed from 55 (8 seconds), not from the premove's anterior instant (13). Mirrors scenario.premove-anchor-never-rewinds with the same numbers
two consecutive chain entries timed before the standing anchor: each charges zero and the anchor holds — it only ever advances
a timing exactly at the anchor charges zero (the boundary case of max(0, timing − anchor)) and leaves the anchor in place
